name: b-blurred-behind-the-nurse
prompt: A tall portrait night photograph taken at bench height in an empty city park, as if on an 85mm lens wide open at f/1.4, focus locked on the nearest face. In the lower foreground, razor sharp, a young nurse in creased navy hospital scrubs sags against the end of an old slatted park bench, head tipped back, eyes closed, mouth slightly open, an ID lanyard knotted and twisted over her shoulder, a crumpled disposable mask hanging from one ear, both hands limp in her lap; fine beads of drizzle cling to her hair and sleeves. The bench is iron and wood, its bottle-green paint flaking away in curls to show orange rust and grey wood grain, rainwater pooled in the slats. Further along the same bench, just behind her shoulder and dissolved by the shallow focus into soft shapes, sits a very fat man in a black frock coat and a tall black top hat: a heavy, smeared dark mass whose only readable details are a pale moon of a face split by a wide white smile and one gloved hand lifted in a lazy backhand wave aimed at her. He is too still, too large, and the eye has to work to be sure he is there at all. A single sodium-vapour streetlamp behind the bench throws a sickly orange glow that blooms into a soft halo in the fine mist, rim-lighting the drizzle and her cheek, while everything outside its pool falls into murky brown-black. The upper third of the frame is wet, empty, starless night sky fading into haze, with no objects in it. Muted palette of sodium orange, bruised umber, wet black and a faint teal in her scrubs; slight film grain, gentle halation around the lamp, no lettering, signs or writing anywhere. Thanks.
